meaning:
ἀπάντησις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀπαντάω), [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;]
usually with seel., ὑπ-; a meeting; εἰς ἀ., with genitive or dative, to meet: Mat.25:6 27:32 (WH, txt., omits), Act.28:15, 1Th.4:17 (see M, Th., in l; M, Pr., 14, 242; MM, VGT, see word; Lft., Notes, 69).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and…
then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air. So we will be with the Lord forever.
